text.paragraph: Establishing care for a known abdominal aortic aneurysm: duplex ultrasound, blood pressure, lipids, smoking, and emergency symptoms. Concerns: An abdominal operation for episodes of abdominal pain found a large swelling of the main artery in his abdomen, which was wrapped rather than repaired; he wants to know its size, how it will be watched, and when an operation would be advised; He has smoked a pipe since his youth and is willing to try to stop; His blood pressure has stayed above target on one medicine. [S]

tr.td: CT angiography of the abdominal aorta and iliac arteries: fusiform infrarenal aneurysm, maximum outer-wall diameter 5.2 cm, beginning 2.0 cm below the lowest renal artery and ending above the bifurcation; neck 2.2 cm wide with 30-degree angulation; moderate mural thrombus; calcified atheroma of the aorta and both common iliac arteries, which measure 1.3 cm; soft-tissue thickening along the front of the aneurysm consistent with the prior wrapping; no periaortic fluid; suprarenal aorta 2.4 cm
Smoking cessation counseling (5 A's), about 15 minutes, with a quit date and nicotine replacement

tr.td: Establishing care for a known abdominal aortic aneurysm: duplex ultrasound, blood pressure, lipids, smoking, and emergency symptoms
Four-week follow-up: CT angiography results, vascular surgery consultation, and a shared decision about repair thresholds
Three-month review: blood pressure, lipids on a statin, and smoking cessation
Six-month aneurysm surveillance with duplex ultrasound
Same-day sick visit for low back pain after lifting

Aneurysm imaging: duplex ultrasound today and CT angiography within two weeks for baseline anatomy; then duplex ultrasound every six months while the diameter is 5.0 to 5.4 cm, with CT if ultrasound views are poor
Vascular surgery consultation for a shared decision about surveillance, repair thresholds, and the choice between endovascular and open repair

Blood pressure below 130/80: add losartan 50 mg to amlodipine, home blood pressure readings twice daily for a week before each visit, and a metabolic panel two to four weeks after each change, then every six months
Atorvastatin 40 mg each evening, with a baseline ALT and a lipid panel four to twelve weeks after starting, then yearly
Tobacco cessation: the 5 A's at every visit, a quit date within a week, a 14 mg nicotine patch with 2 mg lozenges for cravings, stepping down over the following months, and the state quitline

Emergency plan: sudden severe abdominal, back, flank, or groin pain, fainting, or a tender pulsating lump means calling emergency services at once; carry an aneurysm wallet card; avoid fluoroquinolone antibiotics unless there is no alternative
Low-dose aspirin 81 mg daily for atheroma of the aorta, unless bleeding risk outweighs benefit

Shared decision on elective repair: repair advised at 5.5 cm by a consistent measurement, growth of 0.5 cm or more in six months, or symptoms from the aneurysm; endovascular repair favored on this anatomy and after a prior laparotomy with wrapping; his preferences reviewed at each scan

Monitor on the CMID hypertension and hyperlipidemia schedules: blood pressure and weight at every visit; metabolic panel every six months on losartan; lipids, HbA1c, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio yearly; baseline ECG; eye examination yearly; ankle-brachial index every two to three years
Baseline CT angiography and a vascular surgery consultation, with a documented shared decision about repair thresholds, by the four-week visit
CT angiography two weeks after the first visit; consultation and shared decision at the four-week visit
Blood pressure below 130/80 at the clinic and at home by the three-month visit
126/76 mmHg in the clinic; home average 124/74 on amlodipine 5 mg and losartan 100 mg

No tobacco since the quit date a week after the first visit; nicotine replacement finished at six months

5.1 cm, 0.1 cm more than at baseline; next scan in six months
